name: Bulgaria

findings.controller: US Department of State (Clean Network initiative)
findings.local_actor: Ministry of Transport, Information Technology and Communications, Bulgaria
findings.summary: Bulgaria's transport and communications minister and US Under Secretary Keith Krach signed a joint statement on 5G network security, which the US Embassy said brought Bulgaria into the Clean Network coalition against untrusted vendors.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded as a Tier-1 US-aligned statement, not as a Huawei ban: CMS (March 2025) finds no explicit legal ban on Chinese vendors, and the February 2026 NIS2 Cybersecurity Act amendments add only generic supply-chain risk duties. ORF's 'block Chinese equipment' framing overstates a non-binding statement. BTA coded S4 as state news agency.

findings.controller: Nokia (5G RAN); Ericsson (core, per one source)
findings.summary: A1 Telekom Austria group picked Nokia to supply 5G radio access for A1 Bulgaria (with Serbia and Slovenia); one trade report says Ericsson takes the core network.
findings.analyst_inference: Nokia (Finland) and Ericsson (Sweden) are EU-anchored vendors, so third. Economica.net says Nokia supplies core only in Serbia and Slovenia; the Ericsson core claim for Bulgaria rests on Developing Telecoms alone. No value disclosed; tier 3 as a vendor award.

findings.summary: Capital reported that mobile operator Globul, now Yettel Bulgaria, chose Huawei to renew its network.
findings.analyst_inference: Known only from the search-result headline; the page refused fetching (robots). Scope (radio vs core), value and whether Huawei still equips Yettel's 4G/5G network are unconfirmed. Pre-2020 and still_current unknown, so it is halved on the map.

findings.reversal_of: Huawei GSM base-station equipment installed in Vivatel's mobile network
findings.summary: Vivatel said it would remove all its installed Huawei GSM base stations and replace them with Alcatel-Lucent equipment as part of a EUR 32m network upgrade.
findings.analyst_inference: No reason given in the source; coded commercial because nothing points to security or foreign pressure in 2009, which predates the 5G vendor debate. Tier 5 as installed operational equipment. EUR 32m not converted (whole upgrade, not the Huawei portion). A second unopened headline says Nokia won a Vivatel radio and core deal; date unknown.

findings.controller: EuroHPC Joint Undertaking (system owner), hosted by Sofia Tech Park
findings.summary: EuroHPC selected BRAIN++, a EUR 90m AI Factory at Sofia Tech Park built around a new AI-optimised supercomputer, Discoverer++; its EUR 54m hardware tender opened March 2026, closing October 2026, unawarded.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third because the procurement notice says EuroHPC JU (an EU body) will own Discoverer++; Sofia Tech Park is the Bulgarian state host. Tier 2: selection and funded programme, hardware not yet contracted (deadline 16 Oct 2026, award not seen). EUR 90m and EUR 54.2m not converted. Both S1 pages share one issuer; INSAIT is a project partner (S4).

findings.summary: Sofia Tech Park unveiled the Discoverer+ upgrade to its EuroHPC supercomputer: four new HPE servers carrying 32 NVIDIA GPUs, with A1 Bulgaria, Eviden and NVIDIA named as partners.
findings.analyst_inference: Small deployment (32 GPUs) at a nationally significant facility; tier 5 assumes 'unveiled' means operational, which the article does not state. Cost undisclosed. The pending Discoverer++ tender (BGR-005) will decide the much larger accelerator choice.

findings.base_model: Google Gemma 3 series (earlier BgGPT release on Gemma 2 27B)
findings.summary: The National Revenue Agency moved its BgGPT-based assistant from pilot to wider use across its central office and seven territorial directorates, running on its own hardware, with rollout to 7,000+ staff planned via state integrator Information Services.

sources.publisher: European Commission, Interoperable Europe (Public Sector Tech Watch)

findings.analyst_inference: Domestic: INSAIT releases BgGPT weights openly (Apache 2.0) and the NRA runs it locally, so foreign providers cannot switch it off; the US base model is recorded separately. Tier 4 is a judgement: past pilot, not yet full-scale. The EC case study confirms the 2024 NRA pilot but is undated and names no base model.

applications.null_reason: no dedicated search; no safe-city or surveillance procurement surfaced in network, AI-factory or model searches

power.null_reason: only the 2020 US-Bulgaria civil nuclear MOU surfaced, which is not AI- or data-centre-specific

research_gaps: Current RAN/core vendors of Yettel Bulgaria and Vivacom for 4G/5G: is Huawei still in Yettel's network after the 2014 Globul award?
Who wins the Discoverer++ tender (closed 16 Oct 2026) and with which accelerators (NVIDIA vs other)?
Has Bulgaria adopted any binding high-risk-vendor rule under the EU 5G toolbox beyond the 2020 Clean Network statement and NIS2 supply-chain duties?
Safe-city or police video-analytics systems in Sofia or other cities and their vendors were not searched.
Commercial data-centre or AI-campus projects outside Sofia Tech Park (e.g. hyperscaler or Gulf investors) were not searched.
